items.title: For Them, From Me
items.description: Exact artist-approved short caption pending. Do not paraphrase.
items.thesis: I chose these particular objects for my painting because they remind me of everything my parents have endured, every sacrifice they made, every passion they set aside, every dream they quietly let go of. It's also a reminder of my childhood and how they raised me. All of it lingers in the background, aging with time. My parents never stopped moving. They have always been on the run, putting their own needs aside to provide for me. This painting is not just a representation of them; it is a way to preserve a part of who they are. My parents gave up so much of their own creativity so that I could embrace mine. I am a painter today because they gave me the opportunity to become one. Through this painting, I want to freeze a piece of their life to show them all they have done and to remind them of who they are. They were once great at many things — soccer, singing, painting — and above all, they have always been great parents. This work portrays them not just as parents or partners, but as people. This painting is for them to relive their lives, even if just for a little while.

items.title: Chārjon (1 of 4)
items.description: Exact artist-approved short caption pending. Do not paraphrase.
items.thesis:
These paintings have a special place in my heart because they are of my best friends: My cousins. I wanted to paint something outside my comfort zone, since I usually focus on realism. When I came up with this idea of doing something more contemporary, I thought it should feel childlike. My cousins have been such a huge part of my childhood, so I decided to dedicate these paintings to them.

I chose the theme of cats and fish because it comes from an inside joke we had when we were kids. I depicted us as the fish and showed our cat's emotions toward us. It has always been the four of us, and each painting represents one of us. I'm the youngest, and I was always spoiled, they took care of me and taught me everything they learned. Even though I was the youngest, I experienced everything alongside them. Appi and I have siblings who were also included in the paintings, because even though the focus is on the four of us, I still wanted to show our family as a whole.

Time changes everything. In the end, I couldn't leave with them. Now we're all grown up, finding our own paths in life. They've moved to different places in search of who they are, and I'm here painting our childhood together.

items.title: Barely Hanging
items.description: Oil painting of a light fixture — the first object the artist chose for her own room.
items.thesis:
As immigrants from Bangladesh, my family and I lived with very little. There were many of us sharing one roof, and for a long time, having personal space was something I never experienced. Privacy felt like a luxury. My parents worked incredibly hard to eventually buy a house, and for the first time in my life, I had a room of my own.
That space became more than just a bedroom; it became a place where I could explore my creativity, sit with my emotions, and discover who I was without interruption. It was the first place that truly felt like mine.
The painting itself is of a light fixture, and that feels symbolic now. It was the very first thing I chose completely on my own for my room. At the time, it seemed like a small decision, but it represented something much bigger: independence, self-expression, and finally having the freedom to create a space that reflected me.
